classification.difficultyReason: The hardest diagrams require selecting connected triangles and transferring an intermediate angle through successive exterior-angle calculations, sometimes using supplementary or vertically opposite angles.

content.prompt: Use the exterior angle theorem to find $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in each diagram. Give reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ION, with IO extended to P and IN extended to T. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: I,O,P collinear; I,N,T collinear; angle PON=112 degrees; angle ONT=108 degrees; angle INO=alpha; angle OIN=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown symbols are visible.

answer.worked:
Straight angle at $N$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-108^\circ\\\alpha&=72^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle ION$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta&=112^\circ\\72^\circ+\beta&=112^\circ\\\beta&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle HGV with extensions GX and HY. Source blue ordinary lines become black.
spec.mathematics: X,G,V collinear; Y,H,V collinear; angle GHV=65 degrees; angle HVG=40 degrees; angle XGH=gamma; angle YHG=theta.

answer.worked:
Straight angle at $H$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\\theta&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle HGV$:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=65^\circ+40^\circ\\\gamma&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right triangle MNT with sloping sides extended below MT; coordinate-derived right-angle square at N.
spec.mathematics: L,M,N collinear; N,T,S collinear; angle MNT=90 degrees; angle LMT=135 degrees; angle NMT=alpha; angle MTS=beta.

answer.worked:
Straight angle at $M$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-135^\circ\\\alpha&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle MNT$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=\alpha+90^\circ\\\beta&=45^\circ+90^\circ\\\beta&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle AWT and its three printed extensions.
spec.mathematics: A,W,L; C,A,T; W,T,H are collinear triples. Exterior angles at W and A are 130 and 120 degrees. Angle ATH=gamma.

answer.short:
$\gamma=110^\circ$.

Use straight angles at $W$ and $A$, then the exterior angle theorem.
answer.worked:
Straight angles at $W$ and $A$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AWT&=180^\circ-130^\circ\\\angle AWT&=50^\circ\\\angle WAT&=180^\circ-120^\circ\\\angle WAT&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle AWT$:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=50^\circ+60^\circ\\\gamma&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC with ZAC, ABX and YCB straight.
spec.mathematics: Angle ZAB=151 degrees; angle CBX=119 degrees; exterior angle YCA=theta.

answer.short:
$\theta=90^\circ$.

Use straight angles at $A$ and $B$, then the exterior angle theorem.
answer.worked:
Straight angles at $A$ and $B$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAB&=180^\circ-151^\circ\\\angle CAB&=29^\circ\\\angle ABC&=180^\circ-119^\circ\\\angle ABC&=61^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=29^\circ+61^\circ\\\theta&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: AFS with internal LS and extension AG. Curved callouts target the narrow angle at F and angle LSA.
spec.mathematics: G,A,L,F collinear; angle LFS=30 degrees; angle FSL=63 degrees; angle LSA=24 degrees; angle ALS=alpha; angle GAS=beta.

answer.short:
$\alpha=93^\circ$, $\beta=117^\circ$.

Apply the exterior angle theorem first to $\triangle FLS$, then to $\triangle ALS$.
answer.worked:
Exterior angle of $\triangle FLS$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=30^\circ+63^\circ\\\alpha&=93^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle ALS$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=\alpha+24^\circ\\\beta&=93^\circ+24^\circ\\\beta&=117^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three rays GA, GI and GL below a horizontal line ordered S,A,I,L,N. Callout arrows retain their two distinct angle targets.
spec.mathematics: Angle AGI=30 degrees; angle IGL=20 degrees; exterior angle GLN=115 degrees; angle AIG=alpha; exterior angle SAG=beta.

answer.short:
$\alpha=85^\circ$, $\beta=115^\circ$.

Find the angle at $L$, then apply the exterior angle theorem in the two smaller triangles.
answer.worked:
Straight angle at $L$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle GLI&=180^\circ-115^\circ\\\angle GLI&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle GIL$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=65^\circ+20^\circ\\\alpha&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle AGI$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=85^\circ+30^\circ\\\beta&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle HFE, internal GE and HE, and all three extensions. Curved 20-degree callout targets GEH.
spec.mathematics: I,H,G,F collinear; F,E,D collinear; G,E,T collinear; angle IHE=125 degrees; angle TED=32 degrees; angle GEH=20 degrees; angle HGE=alpha; angle HFE=beta.

answer.short:
$\alpha=105^\circ$, $\beta=73^\circ$.

Use exterior angles in $\triangle EGH$ and $\triangle EFG$, with vertically opposite angles at $E$.
answer.worked:
Exterior angle of $\triangle EGH$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+20^\circ&=125^\circ\\\alpha&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
Vertically opposite angles at $E$ give $\angle GEF=32^\circ$.

Exterior angle of $\triangle EFG$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+32^\circ&=\alpha\\\beta+32^\circ&=105^\circ\\\beta&=73^\circ\end{align*}$$
